title: Creating Diffusion Tensor Images (DTI)
author: Laurel Dieckhaus
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6x2hfqe

steps.title: Open terminal
steps.instruction: Open a new terminal window on the Ubuntu system.

steps.title: Create data directory
steps.instruction: Create a directory to store the project data, e.g., `mkdir ~/Data/Projects/`.

steps.title: Enter project directory
steps.instruction: Change to the directory you will use with `cd <directory_path>`.

steps.title: Locate and copy raw files
steps.instruction: Identify the raw diffusion‑weighted files (required types: Bvals, Bvecs, data.img, data.hdr*). List the source location with `ls`. Then copy the needed files to the project directory, e.g., `cp /source/path/*Bvals* /source/path/*Bvecs* /source/path/data.img* /source/path/data.hdr* .`

steps.title: Convert file formats
steps.instruction: Run MRtrix3 conversion with `mrconvert <input> <output>` to change the raw files into the desired format.

steps.title: Import NIFTI to TORTOISE list
steps.instruction: Use the TORTOISE command `ImportNIFTI` to import the NIFTI data; a new folder named `____proc` will be created automatically.

steps.title: Enter processing folder
steps.instruction: Change into the newly created `____proc` directory (`cd ____proc`).

steps.title: Correct motion with DIFFPREP
steps.instruction: Execute the TORTOISE command `DIFFPREP` to correct motion, remove Gibbs ringing, and denoise the data (note: this step is time‑ and core‑consuming).

steps.title: Open file in ITKsnap
steps.instruction: Launch ITKsnap and open one of the processed files for segmentation.

substeps.instruction: Select the Active Contour (Snake) segmentation mode from the toolbar.
Adjust the lower and upper thresholds so the blue mask covers the desired region (keep defaults if possible).
Place the cursor at the centre of the object of interest and click **Add bubble at cursor** to create a red seed; repeat for additional objects if needed.
Press the **Play** button to grow the seed within the mask; verify that the red region fills the entire area of interest across all planes.
When the region is completely filled, click **Finish**.
Press **Update** (lower‑left corner) to view the new 3D segmentation.
From the **Segmentation → Save As** menu, save the mask as `__mask.nii.gz`.

steps.title: Verify working directory
steps.instruction: In the terminal, confirm the current directory with `pwd`.

steps.title: Estimate diffusion tensor and B0
steps.instruction: Run `EstimateTensorNLLS -i ___DTI_DMC.list -m ___mask.nii` which generates `___N1_DT.nii` (diffusion tensor) and `___DT_AM.nii` (B0 amplitude).

steps.title: Compute all tensor maps
steps.instruction: Execute `ComputeAllTensorMaps.bash ___N1_DT.nii` to create all tensor‑derived maps, including `___DEC.nii`.

steps.title: Visualize DEC map
steps.instruction: Open `___DEC.nii` in ITKsnap, open the Layer Inspector, set the Display mode to **RGB**, then press **Update** to view the colour‑coded diffusion‑tensor image.
